title: "THE ABDUCTION OF HELEN" FAN
medium: Ivory, mother-of-pearl, silk, glass, silver; oil paint, inlay, plain weave ribbon, jewel, rivet
medium_parts: oil paint, inlay, plain weave ribbon, jewel, rivet
identifying_description: Guards of ivory with oil paint and inlaid mother-of-pearl, and sticks of ivory with oil paint and applied mother-of-pearl, showing the abduction of Helen of Troy. Chinoiserie figures at bottom. On reverse, a landscape with men arriving in boats, women on shore, a shepherd playing a flute, and a man carrying a knapsack. Sticks and guards secured at top by painted silk plain weave ribbon. Mother-of-pearl thumb guard, and glass jewel and silver rivet.
web_text: Brisé fans imitating Japanese court fans (hiogi) were introduced to Europe via China in the late sixteenth century. Hiogi were folding fans made of thin strips of wood, usually cypress, which were pierced and held together by a rivet at one end. Ivory brisé fans were common in the first quarter of the eighteenth century, with their smooth sticks allowing for vivid painted designs. This fan is lavishly ornamented with painted floral and geometric motifs, several small portraits, and a gripping scene at center, which shows the abduction of Helen of Troy.
